clue.text: Odds arise oddly, off and on

definitions.note: the verges of a road are where a driver pulls off the carriageway and gets back on it

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler notices that the betting odds keep cropping up in a strange, intermittent fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' and 'oddly' tempt you to take odd letters, but 'oddly' is the anagram signal for all nine letters of ODDS ARISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verges beside a carriageway are the places a motorist pulls off onto and rejoins traffic from, so the phrase loosely describes them.

clue.text: Having outfit with new hat, sat on nail and was absolutely OK

parts.note: to rig is to fit out, and a rig is an outfit

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters of hat are remade in another order

parts.note: taken as written
to rivet is to fasten as with a nail; a rivet is a kind of metal pin

explanation.surface: Someone in fresh clothes with an unfamiliar hat sat on a nail and claimed to be perfectly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A trivet is a three-legged stand, proverbially steady; 'new' is the anagram signal for the hat alone, while 'with' and 'on' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in perfect health or order, so it means completely fine.

clue.text: See 1
Mad fellow in grass is breaking up

indicators.note: in places the mad fellow within the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is slang for to inform on someone, which is to sing
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A lunatic lying in the lawn is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is the verb, informing on someone (SING), not the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering is smashing into pieces, a synonym for breaking up.

clue.text: I leave old date for old city ruin

indicators.note: leave means the letter I departs from the word for the old date

parts.note: the Ides were dates in the ancient Roman calendar
Troy was the ancient city besieged by the Greeks

explanation.surface: Someone abandons an ancient appointment to visit a historic ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to ruin it; both are verbs of wrecking.

clue.text: The last way to tax?

indicators.note: way here means manner, so the words the last are put a different way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about the final resort open to a government wanting revenue.
explanation.walkthrough: A stealth tax is one levied quietly so voters do not notice; the clue suggests it is the last method left.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth taxes are the covert sort of levy, so secrecy is a method of taxation.

clue.text: Footballers and economists shouldn't play it

definitions.text: Footballers and economists shouldn't play it

parts.words: Footballers and economists shouldn't play it
parts.note: sportsmen should not cheat by playing dishonestly, and economists should avoid a saving that ends up costing more

explanation.surface: Advice that a certain kind of game is off limits to sportsmen and economists alike.
explanation.walkthrough: To play false is to cheat; a false economy is a saving that costs more in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The word pairs with play to mean cheating and with economy to mean a misguided saving, which both groups should avoid.

clue.text: High quality garment on one entering in the distance

indicators.note: entering puts the garment and one inside the word for distant

parts.note: something in the distance is far away

indicators.note: on means the garment follows one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: A fancy item of clothing worn by someone appearing on the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels and restaurants rated with the top number of stars are of the highest quality.

clue.text: Old country girl in family dialogue

indicators.note: in shows the answer lies within the words family dialogue

explanation.surface: A rural lass of earlier times figures in a household conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: an ancient kingdom of Asia Minor and a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia was an ancient kingdom in Asia Minor and is also a woman's name, like Lydia Bennet in Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Note for a song before solvers died seeing well

parts.note: E is a musical note
a glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices
ye is an old word for you, the solvers
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tune written for a song before the puzzle-doers passed away, with sharp vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen-sighted spots things clearly, so they see well.

clue.text: Fruit of a 5 a month back

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
Aug is the short form of August

explanation.surface: A recipe of a fruit made from a fifth part and a month's worth, run in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5 down but simply means V; 'back' turns AVAUG round.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit of the myrtle family.

clue.text: Woman kept by journalist enters hard work with toy animal

indicators.note: enters puts the journalist piece inside the word for hard work

parts.note: a slog is hard tiring work

indicators.note: kept by means the woman is held inside the journalist

parts.note: ED is the short form of editor, a journalist
Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: A woman looked after by a reporter takes on a heavy job involving a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeve dog was a lapdog, such as a small Pekingese, small enough to be carried in a sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog small enough to carry in a sleeve is a toy breed, a pet kept for its smallness.

clue.text: Become a dove and risk going down

definitions.meaning: to change into a turtle dove, read literally
the phrase means to capsize, as a boat may when it rolls over

explanation.surface: A peacemaker taking a chance on sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a vessel overturns, and read literally it means changing into a turtle dove.

clue.text: He and I may prove Trotsky wrong and effect redistribution

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people may show the Russian revolutionary was mistaken by sharing wealth more fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: The campaign slogan from 2005 called for an end to global poverty; 'and' only joins the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending want across the world would require spreading wealth more fairly, so the slogan amounts to redistribution.

clue.text: On cloud nine a tree must get mutilated as soon as possible: sap, anybody?

parts.note: the ash is a tree

indicators.note: mutilated means cut about, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree is to be hacked about quickly while someone asks who wants its sap.
explanation.walkthrough: A sandboy, an old seller of sand, was proverbially cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on cloud nine is being blissfully content, which is what this simile describes.

clue.text: See 12
Lawman finds gingerbread's available

parts.note: parkin is a sticky ginger cake from northern England; the possessive adds the S
on means available, as in a dish being on

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that the ginger cake is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: C. Northcote Parkinson formulated Parkinson's Law, that work expands to fill the time available.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of a famous law about bureaucracy is a man known for a law, so a lawman.

clue.text: See 12
This bug hunter is nothing more than a North African schismatic

indicators.note: more than means placed above, which in a down clue puts the first piece on top

parts.note: O is nought, nothing
the Donatists were a schismatic Christian sect in Roman North Africa

explanation.surface: A collector of insects is merely a heretic from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: An odonatist studies dragonflies and damselflies, insects loosely called bugs.

clue.text: A nut-eating beetle goes back round building

indicators.note: goes back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse
eating puts the nut inside the beetle

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle

explanation.surface: An insect that feeds on nuts retreats round a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, usually domed.

clue.text: Blower raising 4's city's king detailed to turn politician

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so reversed
detailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the answer to 4 down includes Troy, whose king was Priam
a U-turn is a complete turnaround
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A gust lifting the ruler of an ancient city, ordered to switch to politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Priam minus his tail gives PRIA, upturned AIRP.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that pumps air blows it, so it is a blower.

clue.text: Fish etc with return of a point in the ground

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the ground

parts.note: sod is turf, the ground

indicators.note: return of means the words of a point are read backwards

parts.note: E for east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Fish and other dishes where something comes back to a point in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: OFAE (of, a, E) reversed gives EAFO inside SOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and shellfish taken as food are seafood, hence the etc.

clue.text: See 13
State — or don't — say the extent of my debt?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard, not written

parts.note: stating how much I owe begins I owe a, and then the sum

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to declare how much they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or don't' plays on the alternative: state the amount I owe, or leave it blank after the words I owe a.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a state of the USA in the Midwest.

clue.text: Promise to include student with everything

indicators.note: to include means the student goes inside the promise

parts.note: giving your word is promising
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pledge to admit a pupil along with all else.
explanation.definitionFit: The world is everything there is, all the universe.

clue.text: Thou — quietly — not upright?

parts.note: a thou is slang for a thousand pounds, as is a grand
piano is the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A biblical address delivered softly, suggesting someone dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thou' looks like the old pronoun but is a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is the horizontal piano, in contrast to an upright one.

clue.text: One who has a point in divorce centre turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, reversed
in places the point within the divorce centre

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces
W for west is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A person with a valid argument in a divorce court that shows up.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is one who possesses something, one who has it.

clue.text: See 6
Outstanding digital problem

definitions.meaning: something that sticks out like a ... is conspicuous

explanation.surface: Remarkable trouble with a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom stick out like a sore thumb means to be conspicuous, and literally it is an injured finger.

clue.text: 6 across remark in article that's different

indicators.note: in places the remark inside the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the answer to 6 across, a false remark, is a lie

explanation.surface: A dishonest comment in a piece of writing that stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or strange, different from what is familiar.

clue.text: Low point of polar atmosphere encompassing the end of the world

parts.note: N for north, a pole

indicators.note: encompassing means the air surrounds the last letter of world

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of world

explanation.surface: The bottom of the Arctic atmosphere surrounds the edge of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: One who sticks around may change the man with the money

indicators.note: around means the sticker surrounds the anagram

parts.note: a paster is one who pastes, so sticks

indicators.note: change means the letters of may are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person who stays put may alter the moneyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the official who pays out wages.
